_comment_contexts: These names must match the check names GitHub sees on a PULL REQUEST head
commit, which are not always what the same job is called on a push to main
(`absorption / absorption rules` on a PR vs `absorption` on a push).
DELIBERATELY ABSENT, each for a reason:
CodeQL          an ORPHAN. Code-scanning default setup reports
`not-configured`, but a stale check of that name still
reports and now hard-fails with '1 configuration not
found'. Requiring it would block every PR forever. Our
real one is `static-security / CodeQL (javascript-
typescript)`, which IS required below. See issue #37.
build, unit,    ALL gated on change detection (`if: docs-only == false`),
supply-chain,   exactly like e2e and perf. Requiring a job that CANNOT run
e2e, perf       on a docs-only PR makes such a PR unmergeable forever, and
it did: #55 sat blocked for two weeks — the 'a required
gate can lock out its own repair' PR, locked out by a
required gate. e2e and perf were already excluded for this
reason; the same reasoning simply was not carried to the
other three.
NOT A WEAKENING. `gate coverage (read me)` is required, runs
`if: always()`, `needs` every one of them, and fails on any
`failure` or `cancelled`. A red build still blocks the merge
through it. What is removed is only the unsatisfiable case:
a job that was deliberately SKIPPED can no longer hold a PR
hostage. Residual risk, named: if change detection wrongly
skips a job, coverage passes. The filter is code and the
absorption guard watches for gauntlet weakening.
CodeRabbit,     third-party integrations. Not ours, so not a gate we get
Vercel,         to call non-negotiable.
scorecard
_comment_reviews: required_approving_review_count is 0 because this is a ONE-DEVELOPER repo.
GitHub does not allow you to approve your own pull request, so requiring 1
approval on a solo repo is unsatisfiable: every PR would be permanently
unmergeable except by --admin bypass, which would turn the whole protection
config into theatre. The automated gauntlet is the reviewer here.
RAISE THIS TO 1 (and re-enable require_code_owner_reviews) the day a second
person gets write access. Everything else stays maximally strict.
_comment_signing: required_signed_commits is deliberately ABSENT, not forgotten. Enabling it
while commit.gpgsign is unset rejects every subsequent push INCLUDING the
one that would fix it. The work is key generation + GitHub upload + local
git config, none of which is a repo setting. Tracked as issue #39, and it
gets added here only after a commit shows Verified on github.com.
